description:
Demand gates BinaryOp/UnaryOp operands on RESULT liveness
(src/compiler2/jobs/runtime_demand.rs:2170-2180):

    LoweredStep::BinaryOp { value, left, right, .. } => {
        if !take_live_demand(live, *value).is_ignore() {
            note_live_demand(world, out, live, *left, RuntimeDemand::whole());
            note_live_demand(world, out, live, *right, RuntimeDemand::whole());
        }
    }

but EMISSION is unconditional (src/compiler2/jobs/backend.rs:1887-1897): both
steps map straight to `BackendStep::BinaryOp`/`UnaryOp` with no
`construction_step_or_omitted` gate. That helper (backend.rs:1979) is applied
only to the six fresh-construction steps -- Tuple, List, Map, MapUpdate, Struct,
Bitstring (backend.rs:1823-1868).

So an `Ignore`-demanded result leaves its operands unmaterialized while the step
is still emitted: the fz-9in shape, one step kind over.

## Could not reproduce -- six attempts, all correct

- unused `_z = 10 / d` in an allocating callee beside `Enum.take` -- the op
  EXECUTED (operands were materialized), so no starvation
- `t == u` over two locally-built tuples
- `[9|xs] == xs`
- `range == range` beside `Enum.take` (the exact fz-9in shape)
- `%{a: 1} == m`
- a bare `r == r` expression statement in a separate callee taking a Range param

All printed the expected `[0, 1]` / `[1, 2, 3]` on interp and, where run, JIT.

So the acceptance criterion is still unmet in BOTH directions: neither a repro
nor a proof of unreachability. Keep it as a first-place-to-look note, and do not
spend budget hunting a repro speculatively -- fz-6fr already failed to build one
for the sibling case.

## Two notes for a future probe

- The probe commit the old ticket cites (2b5451677) is NOT reachable in this
  squashed history.
- Its parenthetical `!m` is not fz syntax (`` `!` is not an operator; use `not`
  ``), so that operand form has to be spelled differently.

## Checks

Either a fixture where an Ignore-demanded BinaryOp/UnaryOp result leaves its
operands unmaterialized and the emitted step faults, or a written argument that
the combination is unreachable by construction -- with the reason recorded at
backend.rs:1887 so the asymmetry with the construction steps is explained
in place rather than rediscovered.
title: BinaryOp/UnaryOp steps are emitted unconditionally while demand gates their operands on result liveness
